Irregular verbs and past questions remain inconsistent; should / shouldn't and comparatives/superlatives were functionally available, while some health vocabulary remained more receptive than spontaneous.

classReports.title: Class Report - 18 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: This lesson worked as a welcome-back and personalization class. Gustavo spoke about vacation, travel, football, games, Flight Simulator, sports routines, school subjects, pets and technology. The class helped identify the topics that most naturally motivate him to speak English.
classReports.teacherInsight: Gustavo showed high engagement and a strong willingness to communicate. Personalized topics helped him attempt spontaneous answers and accept teacher support positively.

classReports.title: Class Report - 25 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: The second lesson connected Gustavo's interests with school support. He discussed school subjects, demonstrated Flight Simulator, practiced Past Simple forms, worked with the numbers fifteen and fifty, and completed guided reading/listening around a travel story.
classReports.teacherInsight: Gustavo showed clear progress using Past Simple orally, especially with I went and I didn't..., and benefits from controlled recycling to build accuracy and confidence.

classReports.title: Class Report - 01 Sep 2026
classReports.summary: The third lesson provided important new evidence about Gustavo's grammatical development. The Simple Past is beginning to emerge as a productive resource for communication. Gustavo can access past-tense forms, although irregular verbs and past questions remain inconsistent. The lesson also showed functional access to should / shouldn't and relatively good availability of comparatives and superlatives. Health-related vocabulary showed a distinction between receptive and productive knowledge.
classReports.teacherInsight: The lesson strengthens the conclusion that Gustavo is progressing within CEFR A2 toward B1, with grammatical retrieval and automaticity becoming increasingly important development targets. This is developmental movement, not a CEFR level transition.

grammarOverview.title: Grammar Overview (Cumulative)
grammarOverview.summary: Gustavo is moving from recognition toward productive use. Simple Past is the clearest current indicator: the form is available, but retrieval and automaticity are still developing.
focusPoints: Simple Past: developing → emerging productive control; increase automatic retrieval and consistency.
Irregular past forms: developing; recycle high-frequency forms in meaningful contexts.
Past questions: developing; repeat Did + subject + base verb through real-experience question-answer cycles.
Should / shouldn't: functional / emerging control for advice and recommendations.
Comparatives & superlatives: available with relatively good functional access.
Accuracy without interrupting fluency: maintain communication while improving form.

teacherFeedback.title: Feedback do Professor
teacherFeedback.body: Gustavo está construindo uma base funcional de comunicação e começa a demonstrar maior capacidade de produzir estruturas gramaticais durante a interação. O desenvolvimento mais significativo observado neste ciclo é o início do uso produtivo do passado. Neste momento, o objetivo não deve ser acelerar a introdução de novos conteúdos, mas consolidar estruturas que estão começando a se tornar produtivas. O trabalho com Simple Past, verbos irregulares e perguntas no passado deve continuar integrado a situações comunicativas.

teacherFeedback.title: Teacher Feedback
teacherFeedback.body: Gustavo is building a functional communication base and is beginning to demonstrate greater ability to produce grammatical structures during interaction. The most significant development in this cycle is the emergence of productive past-tense use. At this stage, the priority should not be to accelerate the introduction of new content, but to consolidate structures that are becoming productive. Simple Past, irregular verbs and past questions should continue to be practiced through meaningful communication.

cumulativeImpact.title: Longitudinal Change — Lessons 1–3
cumulativeImpact.summary: A2 functional communication → increasing productive grammatical control → progression toward B1. Lesson 3 adds developmental evidence but does not justify declaring B1 achieved.
evidence: 3/3 completed lessons confirmed: 18 Aug, 25 Aug and 01 Sep 2026.
Functional A2 communication is established in familiar contexts.
Simple Past is beginning to move from studied knowledge toward productive use.
Retrieval speed and consistency, especially irregular forms and past questions, remain the main limiting factor.
Should / shouldn't and comparatives/superlatives are functionally available.
